items.desc: Swollen Narayani and Saptakoshi rivers submerge hundreds of homes in Nawalparasi West and Saptari, forcing rescues. Landslides and road erosion cut off vital routes, including Prithvi and BP highways.

items.title: For 26 years, India has searched passengers at Kathmandu airport. Nepal can’t say why
items.desc: The screening, which has run since the IC814 hijacking, was made public by India, including a record in its parliament, in 2000. In Kathmandu, three separate government agencies say they can’t find a clear paper trail authorising the practice.

items.title: Finance Minister Wagle leaves for Doha
items.desc: Wagle is expected to seek support for post-flood reconstruction and climate finance while advancing infrastructure projects with the multilateral lender.

items.title: India’s election commission orders review of voter-roll changes
items.desc: The review follows reports that election commissioners questioned Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over voter-list changes that allegedly excluded millions of voters.

items.title: Chief Ministers to gather in Biratnagar to discuss challenges of federalism
items.desc: The two-day meeting will explore inter-provincial trade and investment, legal hurdles and coordination with local and federal governments.

items.title: Vegetable prices skyrocket in Valley as landslides disrupt transport
items.desc: Arrivals have fallen by nearly two-thirds since Thursday as highways to major vegetable-producing districts are damaged in places, leading to a steep price rises.

items.title: As rain returns, flood survivors endure cold—and leaking tents
items.desc: Damp weather has raised health concerns for infants and vulnerable groups as permanent resettlement plan awaits central government approval.

items.title: Dhap Dam remains fully safe, says energy ministry
items.desc: The dam’s water level has fallen by 2.38 metres after authorities began releasing water following a landslide near a saddle dam.

items.title: Balendra Shah should prepare for the worst
items.desc: The prime minister cannot afford to spend his first year fighting battles within the party that put him in office.

items.title: Shah returns from UNGA after putting climate crisis at centre of Nepal’s global pitch
items.desc: Nepal’s prime minister highlighted the Bhotekoshi floods, climate justice and Himalayan risks at the UN General Assembly, while seeking greater international support for resilience and reconstruction.

items.title: Koshi floods inundate 157 homes in Saptari
items.desc: Floodwaters entered homes in Tilathi Koiladi and Hanumannagar Kankalini, damaging food stocks and forcing residents to seek shelter on higher ground.

items.title: A month on, Nepal flood victims remain missing as hope and posters fade
items.desc: Relatives plastered hospital walls in Kathmandu with notices searching for loved ones swept away by the Bhotekoshi floods. With thousands still unaccounted for, many families have turned to symbolic last rites.

items.title: From chief minister to shopkeeper, Trilochan Bhatta embraces ordinary life
items.desc: After five years at the helm of Sudurpaschim province, Bhatta has returned to a modest routine behind a grocery shop counter.

items.title: Landslide kills one as heavy rain disrupts life across Nepal
items.desc: Rising rivers, landslides and blocked roads have disrupted communities across several districts, while hundreds of residents have been moved to safer locations.

items.title: NEPSE slips as investors rotate into banks and manufacturing
items.desc: The benchmark index fell 0.66 percent to close at 2,629.81 in a shortened trading week, while average daily turnover edged up to Rs6.12 billion as investors shifted away from hydropower and finance stocks.

items.title: Snow and rain disrupt life across Nepal’s highlands
items.desc: Heavy snowfall and persistent rain have brought colder conditions to high-altitude areas of Jumla, Jajarkot, Gorkha and Manang, affecting residents, livestock and trekkers.

items.title: Washout seals top spot for Nepal. Sri Lanka wait in quarterfinals
items.desc: Nepal’s 149/4 proved enough to top Group A after rain washed out their final preliminary match against Japan, setting up a quarterfinal against Sri Lanka on Tuesday.

items.title: From the Himalayas to the islands, Nepal calls for a united climate response
items.desc: Nepal brings mountain and island nations together under its “Sagarmatha to the Sea” banner to push for climate finance, stronger early-warning systems and deeper cooperation.

items.title: Nepal smash 149 against Japan in rain-shortened Asian Games clash
items.desc: Sandeep Jora and Lokesh Bam hit unbeaten half-centuries as Nepal posted 149 for one in a 15-over-a-side match after rain delayed the start by an hour.

items.title: He got his ear torn for watching TV. Then he went to Cannes
items.desc: Abinash Bikram Shah has spent a lifetime watching films—and eventually began making his own.

items.title: Tashi Gyeltshen on making films, finding freedom and embracing risk
items.desc: The Bhutanese filmmaker talks about his journey from journalism to cinema, the influence of nature and personal memory on his films, and why being self-taught has given him the freedom to take risks.

items.title: What’s on in Kathmandu Valley today
items.desc: From live music and art exhibitions to workshops, debates and a fundraising ride, here are some ways to spend your Saturday.

items.title: One win from the Asian Games quarterfinals, Nepal eye maiden cricket medal
items.desc: Nepal’s five-wicket victory over Afghanistan has put them within reach of the last eight, but the Rhinos must beat hosts Japan on Saturday to keep their medal hopes alive.

items.title: Gulf job opportunities are narrowing for Nepalis
items.desc: New labour approvals have fallen 52 percent since the Iran war began, with some workers sent home on unpaid leave.

items.title: Heavy rains cut off key roads to Kathmandu
items.desc: Travel restrictions imposed on several major highways. Snowfall has disrupted trekking in mountain areas.

items.title: Foreign Minister Khanal gives Nepal a strong voice across UN General Assembly forums
items.desc: With around 40 bilateral and multilateral engagements, the foreign minister has highlighted Nepal’s climate vulnerability and the concerns of developing countries.

items.title: International media highlight Shah’s climate message, regional proposal—and shades
items.desc: Coverage of the prime minister’s UN address has centred on Nepal’s floods, climate justice and a proposed Himalayan climate resilience mechanism.

items.title: Heavy rain disrupts travel, raises flood and landslide risks across Nepal
items.desc: Roads reopen in Taplejung but night travel is restricted in several districts, while rising river levels, damaged homes and snowfall affect communities across the country

items.desc: Can a brilliant UN speech fix Nepal’s climate crisis? (Spoiler: Not without fixing our own backyard)
